title: Sigmoid Prep
subtitle: Sigmoid ML02 · study programme
description: A 10-week preparation programme for the Sigmoid Machine Learning course (ML02): Python, pandas, the maths behind the models, 20 homework notebooks and three timed checkpoints.

labels.projectsIntro: The notebooks from the ML Homework Book, scheduled after the lesson they need. Each counts as done when its link, numbers and written conclusion are in.

phases.title: Phase 1 · Foundations and first models

quiz.q: In `class Student(Human):`, what is `Human`?
o: The parent class Student inherits from
quiz.why: The name in brackets is the parent (base) class. Student gets all of Human's methods and can override them.

quiz.q: Which pandas call gives the mean of every numeric column of `df`?
quiz.why: `DataFrame.mean()` works column by column and returns a Series indexed by column name.

quiz.q: The values 2, 3, 3, 10 have which median?
quiz.why: With an even count the median is the average of the two middle values after sorting: (3 + 3) / 2 = 3.

quiz.q: A Pearson correlation of −0.85 between two columns means:
o: A strong relationship where one goes up as the other goes down
quiz.why: The sign gives the direction and the size gives the strength. Correlation never proves causation.

quiz.q: Why does the handbook add a column of ones to X?
o: So one weight acts as the intercept b
quiz.why: The weight that multiplies the ones column is added to every prediction unchanged, which is exactly the intercept.

quiz.q: A learning rate that is far too large usually makes gradient descent:
o: Converge faster to the exact minimum
quiz.why: Huge steps jump over the valley and can make the cost grow every step.

quiz.q: R² of 0 on the test set means the model:
o: Predicts no better than always guessing the mean
quiz.why: R² = 1 − SSE/SST. When SSE equals SST you are no better than the mean.

quiz.q: Why evaluate on a test set the model never saw?
o: To estimate performance on new data, not memorised data
quiz.why: Training error is optimistic. Held-out data tells you how the model generalises.

quiz.q: Logistic regression outputs 0.73 for a sample. With threshold 0.5 the predicted class is:
Why not use squared error as the cost for logistic regression?
o: Combined with the sigmoid it is not convex and has local minima
quiz.why: The handbook's point: MSE through a sigmoid creates a bumpy cost; log loss stays convex.

quiz.q: A cancer screen should miss as few sick patients as possible. Which metric matters most?
quiz.why: Recall = TP / (TP + FN). Missing a sick patient is a false negative.

quiz.q: 95% of samples are class 0. A model that always predicts 0 has accuracy:
quiz.why: It is right on every class-0 sample, so 95%, while being useless. That is why we also check recall and F1.

quiz.q: Why standardise before PCA?
o: Otherwise columns with big units dominate the variance
It makes the covariance matrix diagonal
quiz.why: PCA chases variance. A salary column in euros would swamp an age column unless both are put on one scale.
Addition rule: 0.3 + 0.5 − 0.1 = 0.7.

quiz.q: What is 'naive' about naive Bayes?
o: It assumes features are independent given the class
quiz.why: That assumption lets the likelihood become a product of one-feature probabilities.

quiz.q: Which naive Bayes suits word-count features?
quiz.why: Multinomial models counts. Bernoulli models present/absent; Gaussian models continuous values.

quiz.q: A bootstrap sample of n rows is drawn:

quiz.q: Why does a random forest also pick a random subset of features at each split?

quiz.q: Fitting a StandardScaler on the whole dataset before splitting causes:

quiz.q: LASSO can select features because its L1 penalty:
o: Drives some weights to exactly zero
quiz.why: The L1 penalty has corners at zero, so weak features get a weight of exactly 0.

quiz.q: SMOTE creates new minority samples by:
